Resolves #19438

Declare native Desktop MCP launch admission as a distinct ADR 0038 credential class. The new §2.5.2 records the approved generation, selected-owner proof, revocation, stopped-profile convergence and truthful recovery contract; existing credential rows remain byte-identical. The architecture guide places class 8 at the local launcher-to-issuer boundary, marked accepted and pending runtime delivery.

Evidence: L1 (static contract and ledger checks) → L1 required (record-only close target). No close-target residuals; runtime and installed delivery remain under neomjs/neo-agent-brain#909 and neomjs/neo-agent-brain#571.

### 🔬 Depth Floor

**Challenge OR documented search (per guide §7.1):**

- **Challenge** (non-blocking, for the implementer's benefit): the provider-secret boundary says provider credentials are "consumed plane-side" and never transit the fleet wire. Class 8's handoff is not the fleet wire, so nothing here is false. But on a Fleet that serves no plane, a resident MC/KB row's bound plan lists its resolved provider keys among `requiredRuntimeEnv` (`bindManagedAgentWorkspacePlan` adds every resolved resident name). Under §2.5.2's "required slots from the bound plan", the class-8 handoff will therefore carry them to that child. A clause saying class 8 may transiently carry a resident server's provider inputs, while they stay adjacent and not a row, would stop a later review from reading the boundary as a ban. Optional; I can also carry it in the JSDoc of neomjs/neo-agent-brain#909.
